title: Raw Pointers
goal: Understand raw pointers and why dereferencing requires unsafe.

source.attribution: adapted from Unsafe Rust: Raw Pointers

sections.text: Rust references always point to valid memory. Raw pointers do not carry this guarantee.

sections.code:
let val: i32 = 42;
let raw_ptr: *const i32 = &val;
sections.caption: Creating a raw pointer from a reference is safe.

sections.text: Immutable raw pointers use `*const T`. Mutable raw pointers use `*mut T`. Creating them is safe.
The compiler does not check if raw pointers are valid. Dereferencing them requires an `unsafe` block.

sections.caption: Dereferencing a raw pointer requires unsafe.

sections.text: Dereferencing invalid pointers causes undefined behavior. You are responsible for memory safety inside `unsafe` blocks.

explanation: Understand raw pointers and why dereferencing requires unsafe.
